subject.title: Feature: Streaming TTS pipeline for voice calls (sentence-level LLM→TTS→audio)

question: Should classic Voice Call adopt a provider-generic streaming speech contract now, and which provider/carrier pair plus fallback semantics should define the first supported implementation?
rationale: The request crosses the plugin speech API, embedded-agent spoken-output boundary, carrier playback lifecycle, provider economics, and recovery behavior; those permanent contracts cannot be selected safely as a mechanical repair.

options.title: Approve phased generic contract
options.body: Add an additive provider-generic stream contract, prove it first with Twilio and ElevenLabs, preserve buffered fallback before any audio is emitted, and add Telnyx through the same contract afterward.

options.title: Use realtime voice only
options.body: Make OpenAI and Gemini full-duplex realtime mode the supported low-latency path and decline a new classic-pipeline streaming API.

options.title: Require plugin-local prototype
options.body: Keep the shared API unchanged until an external voice-call prototype demonstrates latency, interruption, ordering, and failure behavior on a real carrier.

recommendation.title: Approve phased generic contract
recommendation.body: Add an additive provider-generic stream contract, prove it first with Twilio and ElevenLabs, preserve buffered fallback before any audio is emitted, and add Telnyx through the same contract afterward.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history across the voice-call plugin, carrier adapters, telephony TTS, and the separate realtime architecture.
